name: Kind of Blue
description: Miles Davis's landmark 1959 modal jazz album, widely considered the best-selling jazz record of all time.

name: Rumours
description: Fleetwood Mac's 1977 soft rock masterpiece recorded amid personal turmoil within the band.

name: Thriller
description: Michael Jackson's 1982 pop and R&B album, the best-selling album of all time with iconic tracks and music videos.

name: Purple Rain
description: Prince's 1984 soundtrack album blending funk, rock and R&B, accompanying his semi-autobiographical film.

name: Blue
description: Joni Mitchell's intimate 1971 singer-songwriter album exploring love, loss and wanderlust.

name: The Dark Side of the Moon
description: Pink Floyd's 1973 progressive rock concept album exploring themes of conflict, greed, time and mental illness.

name: What's Going On
description: Marvin Gaye's socially conscious 1971 soul album addressing war, poverty and environmental concerns.

name: Nevermind
description: Nirvana's 1991 grunge breakthrough that brought alternative rock to mainstream audiences worldwide.

name: Ready to Die
description: The Notorious B.I.G.'s 1994 debut album cementing East Coast hip-hop's dominance with vivid street narratives.

name: Appetite for Destruction
description: Guns N' Roses' explosive 1987 debut, one of the best-selling hard rock albums ever recorded.

name: Born to Run
description: Bruce Springsteen's 1975 rock epic depicting youth, escape and the American dream on the streets of New Jersey.

name: Songs in the Key of Life
description: Stevie Wonder's sprawling 1976 double album celebrating life in a rich blend of soul, funk and pop.

name: Horses
description: Patti Smith's raw 1975 debut merging punk poetry with rock, opening with a provocative reinterpretation of Gloria.

name: Endtroducing.....
description: DJ Shadow's groundbreaking 1996 album constructed entirely from sampled vinyl, defining instrumental hip-hop.

name: Legend
description: Bob Marley & The Wailers' 1984 reggae compilation, the best-selling reggae album in history.

name: The Velvet Underground & Nico
description: The 1967 debut produced by Andy Warhol, infamous at release but enormously influential on indie and punk rock.

name: Blonde on Blonde
description: Bob Dylan's pioneering 1966 double album blending folk, rock and surrealist lyrics into a new American art form.

name: Dummy
description: Portishead's haunting 1994 trip-hop debut fusing cinematic samples, hip-hop beats and Beth Gibbons's spectral vocals.

name: Innervisions
description: Stevie Wonder's 1973 album featuring socially aware lyrics over complex funk and soul arrangements.

name: Pet Sounds
description: The Beach Boys' 1966 studio masterpiece, an ambitious orchestral pop record that influenced countless artists.

name: A Love Supreme
description: John Coltrane's spiritual 1965 jazz suite dedicated to his faith, recorded in a single session of divine intensity.

name: Logical Progression
description: LTJ Bukem's 1996 drum and bass compilation showcasing atmospheric, jazz-infused liquid jungle sounds.

name: Graceland
description: Paul Simon's 1986 album incorporating South African township music styles, winning the Grammy for Album of the Year.

name: Remain in Light
description: Talking Heads' 1980 art rock album layering African polyrhythms and found-sound textures under David Byrne's anxious vocals.
